audit.why: 53.14% over 207 games. Quinn owns level 1 outright, the lane goes even at 2-3, and Gragas takes it from 4 onward.
audit.corrected: Kept the difficulty framing; the mirror set EVEN 5/10 from its side and the substance now agrees.

audit.whatIsWrong: The stored chart gave Quinn five rows; packet and mirror both read Quinn / Skill / Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Gragas / Skill.
audit.why: The content-layer whys already described exactly that progression — only the win/side tokens disagreed with their own explanations. Gragas's item spike (Rylai/Cosmic Drive) beats Quinn's lethality on a squishy frame.
audit.corrected: All seven rows proposed as one atomic group across both layers, ratings moved with them (L1 6/10, the three Gragas rows 3/10), and every phases[N].why rewritten to match its new side.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Q-blind' / 'Vault-blind' framing; 'Vault away over him'; nothing about Body Slam ending Behind Enemy Lines; no Drunken Rage tell.
audit.why: Blinding Assault hinders vision by Riot's text, it is not a blind and it is a Q not an E. Vault leaps Quinn to max attack range from the target — it does not carry her over him. Body Slam stuns, and Behind Enemy Lines is a flagged channel, so his engage cancels her ultimate. Drunken Rage is a 1-second drink into an empowered auto — the drink is the tell, not the attack.
audit.corrected: Named Body Slam's 14s cooldown and its cancel on the channel, restated Vault's landing, replaced the blind with the nearsight, and made the Drunken Rage wind-up the step-back cue.

audit.why: Happy Hour heals off every cast, and report[8] already carries early Oblivion Orb / Executioner's.
audit.corrected: No change needed; the anti-heal line is already in itemization.

edits.before: Passive-mark AA trades win every short exchange. Identify how Gragas contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: You out-range him and Harrier resets chunk him every time he steps up for a melee last-hit — he has no level-1 answer.

edits.before: Vault resets the spacing whenever he closes. Only take the trade when Gragas's Body Slam is down.
edits.after: Heightened Senses is online but so is Body Slam's 600 range — a coin-flip on which of you commits first.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Gragas must walk into your range.
edits.after: You stack Harrier autos and Blinding Assault, but Happy Hour heals the chip straight back — neither side wins.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Body Slam's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Body Slam into Barrel Roll, with Drunken Rage cutting the damage he takes, soaks your Harrier burst — he out-sustains the poke.

edits.before: Behind Enemy Lines exports your lead — roam on every shove. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Gragas's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Explosive Cask plus a 14s Body Slam gives him the all-in, and that stun cancels Behind Enemy Lines mid-channel. Roam, don't duel.

edits.before: Youmuu's Ghostblade is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Body Slam's cooldown.
edits.after: His Rylai/Cosmic Drive brawl spike out-values your lethality on a squishy frame — the item window is his.

edits.before: Two items on: your pattern is at full power. Gragas carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: A wash: he displaces and sustains in fights while you roam and pick, so whoever snowballed earlier decides it.

edits.before: Track Gragas's Body Slam: His engage. Vault after it. When it is down — Vault-blind + R him.
edits.after: Body Slam is 14s at rank 1 and its stun ends Behind Enemy Lines — channel only after he spends it.

edits.before: That is Gragas's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Drunken Rage's one-second drink is the tell — step back on the wind-up, not the auto.

edits.before: Win levels 1-3 with Harrier auto-resets and Q blind, then shove and roam with R for plates and picks
edits.after: Win levels 1-3 with Harrier autos and Blinding Assault's vision denial, then shove and roam for picks

edits.before: Bait his E body-slam, then E-Vault away over him while refreshing Harrier for a free trade
edits.after: Bait his 14s Body Slam, then Vault to land an attack range away and take the free trade

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are yours. Gragas has to walk into melee CS range, and every time he does your Harrier mark plus a leashed auto chunks him for free — there's no trade he wins back. Use Q to poke when he goes for a body-slam wave clear, and keep E-Vault up purely as your panic button: if he E's onto you, Vault over him to disengage and refresh Harrier rather than spending it offensively. Don't get greedy stacking autos into his Q-pool — that's the only thing that heals his health bar back.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours. Gragas has to walk into melee CS range, and every time he does your Harrier mark plus an auto chunks him for free. Poke with Blinding Assault when he commits Barrel Roll to the wave, and keep Vault purely as your panic button: if Body Slam lands, Vault leaps you a full attack range away, so use it to leave rather than to engage. Don't stack greedy autos inside a live Barrel Roll — Happy Hour heals off every skill he casts, so chip damage you cannot follow up on simply refunds itself.

notes: Gragas's Barrel Roll is a cask that explodes on activation or after 4 seconds and gains potency over time; the inherited 'Q-pool' language treats it as a persistent puddle, which Riot's text does not support. I corrected it where the length band allowed and left the remaining 'Q puddle' strings (dontsFull[1].t, report[11].t) flagged here. Happy Hour is the sustain, not the cask.
